gate.defect: Gate question 3 — the named evidence cannot fail. The new clause asks the suite to assert 'that app.router.lifespan_context is set'. In FastAPI that attribute is always set: an app constructed with no lifespan= gets fastapi.routing._DefaultLifespan, which is a truthy object. Verified in this workspace on the installed FastAPI: FastAPI() gives router.lifespan_context = <fastapi.routing._DefaultLifespan object>, bool() is True; FastAPI(lifespan=ls) gives the function itself. A truthiness or is-not-None assertion therefore passes identically whether or not lifespan= was passed, which is the exact edit this clause was added to catch. The discriminating assertion is identity — app.router.lifespan_context is lifespan — or exclusion of _DefaultLifespan; the prompt's parenthetical 'rather than merely defined' points that way but the literal instruction 'is set' does not require it, and an implementor following the words gets a test that cannot fail. The spec's T5 block carries the same wording, so the fix lands in both. The TICK_SECONDS == 1 half of the same clause is sound and does discriminate.

escalations: T5 re-run refused before dispatch: the assertion added to close O1's other half is satisfied by a FastAPI app that never had a lifespan attached, because lifespan_context defaults to _DefaultLifespan rather than to None.
